comparison_title: Comparative Forensics: Mercado Libre vs Paris Brand Discovery
symptom: BRAND_DISCOVERY FAIL in baseline capability matrix

source_type.Mercado_Libre: Official Brand Store (tienda/nicopoly / _Tienda_nicopoly). All products displayed belong to the brand. SSR rendered by internal Meli stack (Andes UI) with Akamai session protection.
source_type.Paris: Brand Search PLP (search?q=nicopoly). Next.js App Router (RSC streaming self.__next_f / React 18+). Products are returned based on full-text search match.

discovery_mechanism.Mercado_Libre: Subcategories are exposed as sidebar facet filter links (.ui-search-filter-dl dt) within the store scope. No navigation tree endpoint exists.
discovery_mechanism.Paris: Category facets (tipoProductoAll: Abrigos, Blusas, Calzas) and the official brand landing route (/mujer/marcas/nicopoly/) are embedded inside Next.js RSC streaming state (self.__next_f). In the DOM, an uncollapsed site-wide Mega-Menu in <details> tags pollutes generic anchor extraction.

application_mechanism.Paris: PLP query parameter facets (?q=nicopoly&tipoProductoAll=...) or category brand routes (/mujer/marcas/nicopoly/).

verification_mechanism.Mercado_Libre: Quantity counter text (.ui-search-search-result__quantity-results) and seller verification badge ('Tienda oficial').
verification_mechanism.Paris: Facet counts embedded in RSC query state and product card brand text.

evidence: Mercado Libre and Paris share 0 architectural components for brand discovery. ML relies on official store URL rewriting and sidebar DL facets; Paris relies on Next.js App Router RSC streaming state and PLP query parameters. Merging them into a single abstraction would violate Rule 4 (PROHIBIDO crear una abstracción común solamente porque ambos fallan en BRAND_DISCOVERY).
conclusion: ML_PARIS_SAME_MECHANISM = NO. Each marketplace requires its own distinct discovery adapter matching its native rendering and taxonomy architecture.
